newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand's North Island hit by minor tremors.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand's North Island hit by minor tremors.

text.p: Dozens of small tremors swept New Zealand's North Island on Saturday, forcing the evacuation of about 70 tourists, a civil defence spokesman said.
Malcolm Breadmore, civil defence officer in the town of Rotorua, told Reuters there had been "swarms of quakes" measuring up to 3.6 on the Richter scale.
About 70 tourists of various nationalities were evacuated from the Waimangu thermal area southeast of Rotorua.
Breadmore said some tremors were strong enough to crack roads. Damage was minor and no one was hurt.
The Rotorua region is known for its geysers, hot springs and mudpools. Earthquakes were not uncommon.

It was not clear if the tremors were linked to activity at Mount Tarawera, a nearby active volcano that killed 153 people in an eruption in 1886. No unusual activity was visible from the volcano, Breadmore said.
